newsitem.title: USA: LDC debt prices end mixed in light trading.
newsitem.headline: LDC debt prices end mixed in light trading.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices were quoted mostly unchanged to slightly down in light trading as players focused on the IMF meeting in Washington, upcoming debt issues and key U.S. economic data, traders said.
"The market was very inactive today and close to unchanged on most issues," one said. "Volume is light with many investors away at the IMF coupled with Friday's U.S. jobs data."

Investors are expected to key in on the annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank for word on whether or not Bulgaria has won a much delayed second tranche of an IMF loan, crucial to lifting the country out of economic crisis.
In addition, investors are also eyeing two large global debt offerings expected to come to market this week.
Argentina is expected to launch it's $750 million 10-year global debt offering on Tuesday via joint lead managers Goldman Sachs and Salomon Brothers.
Price talk on the issue is in the 435-450 basis points range, although some players predicted a tighter spread of 410-425 basis points.

Brazil is also getting ready to launch $750 million in a five-year or 10-year global debt issue this week, sources said. Traders said Brazil is most likely to lean towards a five-year issue to avoid clashing with Argentina's upcoming 10-year eurobond, sources added.
Price talk on a potential five-year issue is seen around 250 basis points over Treasuries, although some traders said the low 200's was possible.
Meanwhile, in price activity on Tuesday, traders said the market was bid a little better earlier in the day until U.S. Treasuries turned lower.
"Bradies were better bid this morning...then Treasuries turned around and that took the wind out of some of these markets," one trader said.
The U.S. Treasury 30-year bond is off 8/32 at 97-25/32 to yield 6.93 percent.
In the Brady bond market, Argentine Pars were down 1/2 at 58-1/4 bid, while Argentine FRBs were unchanged at 83-3/4.
Meanwhile, Brazilian Cs were up 1/8 to trade at 70-3/8 bid and Brazilian Pars were down 1/8 at 59-1/2 bid.
Bulgaria flrb were off 3/8 at 32-1/2 bid and Bulgaria IAB's traded off 1/8 at 46-1/8.
Venezuela pars were off 3/4 at 69.375 bid
In other issues, Russian Vnesh dollar-denominated paper was off 1/8 to trade at a 69-5/8 bid.
Looking ahead players are expected to key in an Friday's release of September U.S. nonfarm payrolls and unemployment by the Labor Department.
In a Reuter poll, U.S. economists expect September nonfarm payroll to increase by 166,000 and for unemployment to rise slightly to a 5.2 percent rate.
